results.quote: There is an algorithm for CMM with f_E running in time O(N^2), where N := \sum_{v\in V}|v|.

results.bound: No \mathcal{O}(N^{2-\varepsilon} \mathrm{poly}(|E|,|V|)) \text{ algorithm for any } \varepsilon>0 \text{ unless SETH fails}
results.quote: There is no algorithm solving CMM with f_E in time O(N^{2-\varepsilon} \mathrm{poly}(|E|,|V|)), for any \varepsilon>0, unless SETH fails.
There is an algorithm for CMM with f_{\chi^2} running in time O(N^2), where N = \sum_{v\in V}|v|.

results.bound: No \mathcal{O}(N^{2-\varepsilon} \mathrm{poly}(|E|,|V|)) \text{ algorithm for any } \varepsilon>0 \text{ unless SETH fails}
results.quote: There is no algorithm solving CMM with f_{\chi^2} in time O(N^{2-\varepsilon} \mathrm{poly}(|E|,|V|)), for any \varepsilon>0, unless SETH fails.
There is an algorithm for (\ell,d)-CMM with f_E running in time O(\binom{\ell}{d}^2 N^2), where N := \sum_{v\in V}|v|.
(\ell,d)-CMM is W[1]-hard by d for both f_E and f_{\chi^2}.
